results.title: Mirae Asset Sekuritas assesses global pressures still weighing on the market
results.body: Mirae Asset Sekuritas says global sentiment continues to weigh on Indonesia’s market, noting that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.33% to 6,589 amid a net foreign outflow of Rp748 billion. The pressure was most evident on banking stocks BBCA and BBRI, while foreign investors accumulated commodity‑linked shares such as ANTM, AADI, CUAN and PTBA. The firm cites macro factors including the US 10‑year Treasury yield near 5%, the ECB rate at 2.5%, high oil prices, the rupiah at roughly Rp17,547 per USD and a 10‑year SBN yield of 7.11% as limiting the transmission of global yields to the domestic market. Despite these headwinds, consumer confidence rose to 118.5 in August and Mirae Asset recommends a selective portfolio focused on strong fundamentals and solid cash flow.

results.title: IHSG Falls 1.49% in First Session as Global Markets Slide on Oil Surge and Fed Rate Hike Bets
results.body: The Indonesian Composite Stock Price Index (IHSG) fell 1.49% to 6,490 in the first trading session on Friday, driven by heavy selling pressure across the market. Big-cap stocks BYAN, BBCA, and BRMS were the primary weights on the index, while transport, non-primary consumer, and infrastructure sectors led declines of more than 1.7% each. The selloff tracked a broad decline across Asian markets as Brent crude surged above $108 per barrel and stronger-than-expected US producer inflation increased the probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike to 70%. The rupiah weakened to 17,610 per US dollar amid dollar strength fueled by rate hike expectations. Panin Sekuritas cited escalating geopolitical tensions, oil above $100 per barrel, and heavy foreign outflows as key drivers.

results.title: Indonesian rupiah and IHSG pressured by surge in oil prices amid US-Iran tensions.
results.body: The Indonesian stock market (IHSG) fell 1.33% to 6,589.34 and the rupiah weakened 0.2% to 17,547 per US dollar on Thursday, pressured by a surge in Brent crude oil prices above $100 per barrel amid escalating US-Iran tensions. The decline marked the IHSG's lowest level in a week and made it the worst-performing emerging market index in Asia Pacific, with all sectoral indices down, led by energy (-2.06%) and transportation (-1.80%). Trading value reached Rp21.58 trillion with 51 billion shares exchanged, with PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk among the most actively traded stocks. Most Asian emerging market currencies weakened against the dollar, though the Malaysian ringgit and Chinese yuan edged higher.

results.title: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk announces quarterly interim dividend plan for 2026
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk announced that it will pay interim dividends on a quarterly basis in 2026. The next interim dividend of Rp25 per share is scheduled for 16 September 2026, up from Rp20 per share paid in June 2026, with a further interim dividend planned for December 2026. The company reported a dividend payout ratio of 72% for the most recent period, up from 68%, and total profit of Rp29.5 trillion for the first half of 2026, including its subsidiaries. Credit grew 8% year‑on‑year to Rp1,036 trillion and CASA rose 10.2% year‑on‑year to Rp1,082 trillion, supporting the dividend policy.

results.title: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk Reports Credit Growth to Rp1,036 Trillion and NPL Decline to 1.9% in First Half 2026
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BCA) disclosed in its 2026 public expose that credit expanded 8% year-on-year to Rp1,036 trillion as of June 2026, driven by productive credit growth of 11% to Rp802 trillion and corporate lending growth of 13.6% to Rp513.4 trillion. Asset quality improved with the non-performing loan ratio falling to 1.9% from 2.2% a year earlier and the loan-at-risk ratio easing to 4.9% from 5.7%. Third-party funds rose 7.9% to Rp1,284 trillion, supported by a current account savings account (CASA) ratio of 85.2%. The bank and its subsidiaries recorded a net profit of Rp29.5 trillion for the first half of 2026, while green financing grew 19% to Rp123 trillion. Meanwhile, BBCA shares have declined 18.69% year-to-date to Rp6,525.

results.title: BCA Announces Up to Rp5 Trillion Share Buyback Program Running Until March 2027
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk has an ongoing share buyback program of up to Rp5 trillion that runs until March 2027. The company has already repurchased approximately Rp3.5 trillion of shares since last year. The program was approved at the 2026 annual general meeting and covers a 12-month period from March 2026 to March 2027. Management says buybacks will be executed when market conditions are overly volatile to demonstrate confidence in the bank's fundamentals.

results.title: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk to pay interim dividend of Rp25 per share on 16 September 2026
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk announced an interim dividend of Rp25 per share payable on 16 September 2026. The payout is part of a new quarterly dividend policy that will see dividends distributed in June, September, December and a final dividend in March 2027 after the shareholders' meeting. The interim amount is higher than the Rp20 per share paid in June 2026. Under the quarterly schedule, shareholders can expect dividend payments each quarter throughout the 2026 fiscal year.

results.title: IHSG falls 0.58% in first session as foreign investors net sell Rp577 billion, led by PT Bank Central Asia Tbk and PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) declined 0.58% to 6,647.50 in the first trading session on Wednesday (9/9), with total transaction value reaching Rp8.32 trillion. Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp577.21 billion, dominated by bank stocks with the largest market capitalization. PT Bank Central Asia Tbk posted the largest net foreign sell of Rp419.03 billion, followed by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk at Rp62.73 billion. Most sectoral indices weakened, with healthcare down 1.45% and technology down 1%, while transportation gained 2.15%. Regional Asian markets were mixed, with South Korea's KOSPI rising 1.01% and India's NIFTY falling 0.52%.

results.title: Foreign investors net buy hundreds of billions of rupiah in a day, snapping up ten stocks
results.body: On Tuesday, 8 September 2026, foreign investors recorded a net purchase of Rp398.12 billion across the Indonesian stock market. In the regular market segment, net buying reached Rp379.39 billion, with the largest single‑stock net buy of Rp269.68 billion in PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, whose shares rose 0.75% to Rp6,675. PT Bumi Resources Tbk experienced the biggest net sell of Rp178.07 billion, yet its stock gained 2.73% to close at Rp226. The broader market reflected the buying trend, as the Indeks Harga Saham Gabungan (IHSG) closed in the green zone at 6,686 points, up 66.77 points (1.01%).

results.title: IHSG forecast to reach 6,700 amid Anak Krakatau eruption concerns, with BBCA, BBRI, BMRI under pressure and BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommending IMPC, TINS, KOTA, UDNG.
results.body: The article forecasts that Indonesia's composite index (IHSG) could climb to the 6,600‑6,700 range, with a key resistance at 6,700, despite the ongoing Anak Krakatau eruption. On Monday the index slipped 0.25% to 6,619.67, staying above the 20‑day moving average and with a positive MACD, while foreign‑exchange reserves rose to US$146.5 billion supporting domestic sentiment. Technical pressure is coming from BBCA, BBRI and BMRI, whereas BRI Danareksa Sekuritas recommends swing‑trade positions in IMPC and TINS, a day‑trade in KOTA, and a sell stance on UDNG. The market’s near‑term direction may be swayed by the U.S. CPI release on 11 September, projected at 3.4% headline and 2.4% core inflation, which could affect risk appetite and the index’s trajectory.

results.title: IHSG Projected to Remain Limited on Tuesday (Sept 8), Sentiment Overview
results.body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) is projected to trade within a limited range on Tuesday (Sept 8) after closing at 6,619.67, down 16.80 points (0.25%) on Monday, with analysts noting pressure from big‑cap financial stocks BBCA, BBRI and BMRI while health and energy sectors provide support and technical levels suggest support near 6,603‑6,600 and resistance near 6,632‑6,700. Analysts from MNC Sekuritas and BRI Danareksa Sekuritas set target prices for HRUM (Rp 985‑1,015), INKP (Rp 9,250‑9,500), MDKA (Rp 2,980‑3,020) and recommend buying IMPC (Rp 1,605‑1,730), TINS (Rp 4,610‑4,830) and KOTA (Rp 224‑236) as the market watches upcoming NFP, China trade‑balance and US CPI releases and Indonesia’s foreign‑exchange reserves at US$146.5 billion.

results.title: Foreign investors show early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian equities, with analysts highlighting big banks and select sectors.
results.body: Foreign investors are showing early signs of tactical re-entry into Indonesian stocks, with net buying concentrated in large-cap banks during the week of August 31 to September 4, 2026. In that period, foreign net purchases reached Rp1.85–2.3 trillion, led by PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, which together recorded over Rp3.19 trillion of net foreign buying in the regular market. LQ45 outflows have declined sharply from over Rp15 trillion in June to under Rp2 trillion in August, and the number of LQ45 stocks with outflows fell to 27 from 36 in June. Analysts caution this is not yet a structural trend reversal, as year-to-date foreign outflows remain around US$3.94 billion, and sustainability depends on Federal Reserve policy, rupiah stability, and earnings growth. Potential rotation targets include commodity stocks ANTM, AMMN, and INCO, as well as consumer and industrial names TLKM, ASII, INDF, and UNTR, with advisors recommending accumulation on weakness.

results.title: Private Bank Interest Income Sluggish, High-Yield Credit Remains Limited
results.body: The article reports that interest income for Indonesia’s private banks fell in July 2026, while credit growth was driven by low‑yield loans. CIMB Niaga’s interest income dropped 4.83% YoY to Rp 12.67 trillion despite total financing rising 7.79% YoY to Rp 230.65 trillion; Maybank Indonesia’s interest income fell 3.44% YoY to Rp 5.88 trillion; Permata Bank’s interest income declined 8.25% YoY to Rp 9.21 trillion; and SMBC’s interest income fell 6.56% YoY to Rp 7.61 trillion. In contrast, Bank Central Asia’s interest income grew 1.48% YoY to Rp 54.59 trillion as its credit portfolio expanded 8.38% YoY to Rp 1,000.88 trillion. Executives from the affected banks cited weak retail and MSME loan demand, high cost of funds and the recent BI‑Rate increase to 5.75% as key factors limiting high‑yield credit opportunities.

results.title: Foreign Capital Flow to IHSG Intensifies, Up 8 Times Last Week
results.body: Foreign investors’ net buying in the Indonesian stock market surged eightfold last week, with the benchmark index rising 1.82% to 6,636. The bulk of the inflow targeted the country’s largest banks—BBRI, BMRI, BBCA and BBNI—where net purchases reached about Rp1.6 trillion in the regular market during the week of August 24‑28. Over the past month, foreign investors accumulated net purchases of Rp4.64 trillion across all markets, while the banks posted strong first‑semester earnings of Rp31.2 trillion, Rp30.4 trillion, Rp29.5 trillion and Rp10.8 trillion respectively. Credit growth outpaced deposit growth, tightening liquidity and underscoring the importance of monitoring NIM and bank liquidity amid continued foreign inflows.

results.title: Foreign investors heavily buy big bank stocks PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk in the past week.
results.body: The article reports that foreign investors returned to Indonesia’s banking sector last week, posting the largest net purchases in the market for the three big banks. PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk recorded a net buy of Rp 1.41 trillion, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk Rp 1.20 trillion and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk Rp 1.01 trillion, together accounting for about Rp 3.62 trillion of foreign inflows, while PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk added Rp 261.39 billion. Other heavily bought stocks included PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (Rp 238.84 billion), PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (Rp 168.05 billion), PT Triputra Agro Persada Tbk (Rp 147.58 billion), PT Erajaya Swasembada Tbk (Rp 126.94 billion), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (Rp 93.49 billion) and PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (Rp 84.23 billion). Foreign investors sold PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (Rp 485.66 billion), PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (Rp 337.42 billion), PT Indosat Tbk (Rp 225.62 billion), PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (Rp 173 billion), PT Petrosea Tbk (Rp 162.7 billion), PT Astra International Tbk (Rp 150.28 billion), PT Bukalapak.com Tbk (Rp 129.03 billion), PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (Rp 126.97 billion), PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (Rp 121.57 billion) and PT Unilever Indonesia Tbk (Rp 109.91 billion), contributing to a total foreign net buy of Rp 1.85 trillion and supporting a 1.82 % weekly rise in the IHSG index, which closed at 6,636.47, down 31.4 points (0.47 %) on Friday.

results.title: Popular News Roundup: CPIN Earnings Surge, Strong Foreign Buying in BBCA, BBRI and BUMI, and Steady Gold Jewelry Prices
results.body: The roundup highlights PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk’s Q2 2026 net profit soaring 211% YoY to IDR 1.13 trillion while trading at a PER of 7.18×, and strong foreign inflows into PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (IDR 820.2 bn net buy), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (IDR 1.4 trn net buy) and PT Bumi Resources Tbk (IDR 83.2 bn net buy) with target price upside of 41.5% for BBCA and a PBV of 1.9× for BBRI. Gold jewelry prices across various karats remained steady, as reported by Raja Emas Indonesia, Hartadinata Abadi and Laku Emas.

results.title: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk Report Combined Rp 111.67 Trillion Profit
results.body: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk, the four largest banks in Indonesia and members of the KBMI 4 group, posted a combined net profit of Rp 111.67 trillion for January–July 2026, an 8.73% year‑on‑year increase. In the same period they expanded credit to Rp 5,017.30 trillion (up 16.95% yoy, representing 55.93% of national credit) and total deposits to Rp 5,693.98 trillion (up 15.71% yoy, accounting for 58.90% of total deposits), outpacing industry averages of 13.0% and 7.7% respectively.

results.title: KB Valbury Sekuritas maintains buy rating on PT Bank Central Asia Tbk with Rp 9,480 target price implying 41.5% upside
results.body: KB Valbury Sekuritas kept a buy recommendation on PT Bank Central Asia Tbk and set a target price of Rp 9,480, representing a 41.5% premium to the September 4 close of Rp 6,700. The target reflects a 3.8 times price-to-book valuation for 2026 projections versus the current 2.6 times, suggesting re-rating potential if positive catalysts materialize. Foreign investors net bought Rp 820.2 billion of BBCA shares during August 31 to September 4, 2026, following Rp 386.5 billion of net buying the prior week, while the stock has gained 3.4% weekly and 6.3% monthly despite a 17% year-to-date decline. Key catalysts cited include stronger-than-expected loan growth and yield, lower cost of credit, and improving domestic and global sentiment. Risks flagged include weaker loan growth, higher funding costs and cost of credit, deeper net interest margin compression, and rupiah depreciation against the US dollar.

results.title: Indonesia's gigawatt-scale data centre expansion requires financing beyond bank lending, experts say
results.body: Indonesia's target to reach 1.7 gigawatts of data centre capacity by 2026 translates to an estimated US$17 billion investment need, which industry leaders say exceeds the lending capacity of banks alone. Recent syndicated loans include Rp6.7 trillion from Bank DBS Indonesia and Bank UOB Indonesia for the DayOne-INA campus in Batam, Rp17 trillion from PT Bank Central Asia Tbk for PT DCI Indonesia Tbk in May 2026, and Rp8.8 trillion from a syndicate of PT Bank OCBC NISP Tbk, PT Bank HSBC Indonesia, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk for STT GDC Indonesia in June 2026. JPMorgan Indonesia CEO Gioshia Ralie states that bank financing has inherent limits and must be combined with capital market instruments, a view echoed by IDPRO Chairman Hendra Suryakusuma, who notes that bank loans remain crucial for construction but that operational assets can attract institutional investors, infrastructure funds, and green financing. Gioshia adds that this blended financing model is already established in the United States and can be replicated in Indonesia.

results.title: Big Four Stocks Weaken Today, Check Recommendations for Next Week
results.body: On September 4, 2026, the Big Four Indonesian banks—PT Bank Central Asia Tbk, PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk—experienced intraday declines of 1.11%, 0.90%, 0.59%, and 0.51% respectively, closing at Rp 6,700, Rp 4,420, Rp 3,390, and Rp 3,940 per share. Despite the day‑to‑day weakness, the banks had gained 3.47%, 4.00%, 4.23%, and 6.27% over the past week. Analyst M. Nafan Aji Gusta of Mirae Asset Sekuritas Indonesia recommends accumulating purchases of PT Bank Mandiri Tbk at a target price of Rp 4,720, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk at Rp 7,900, and PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk at Rp 4,020, citing solid credit growth and a supportive rupiah. The article also notes that the sector’s 13% year‑on‑year credit expansion and risk‑on sentiment from a stronger rupiah underpin the banks’ resilience.
